q: You enable the storage account firewall and add VNet1/SubnetA. VMs in SubnetA still cannot reach the storage account. The most likely missing step is:
opts: The Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on SubnetA
A public IP on each VM
exp: VNet firewall rules require the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on the subnet. A private endpoint is a different mechanism.

q: After enabling the storage firewall with 'selected networks', Azure Backup and some Microsoft services stop working. Which setting fixes this without opening the account to the internet?
opts: Allow trusted Microsoft services to access this storage account
exp: The trusted Microsoft services exception lets selected Azure services through the firewall.

q: You administer the storage account from your office (public IP 203.0.113.10) while the firewall is enabled. What do you add?
opts: A VNet rule for your office
Your office public IP (or range) to the firewall's IP address rules
A private endpoint at the office
exp: Public IP ranges go in the firewall IP rules. VNet rules are for Azure subnets.

q: Which SAS fields limit a token so that it works only from a given IP range and only over HTTPS?
exp: SAS supports signedIp and signedProtocol (HTTPS only) restrictions.

q: You issued ad-hoc service SAS tokens valid for 1 year. One token leaked. How do you revoke it?
opts: Regenerate the account key that signed it (this invalidates all SAS signed with that key)
Remove the user from Entra ID
Set the blob tier to Archive
exp: An ad-hoc SAS can't be revoked individually; regenerating the signing key kills it (and all others signed with that key). Use stored access policies to avoid this.

q: What is the main benefit of creating SAS tokens from a stored access policy?
opts: You can modify or revoke the policy afterwards, which immediately affects all SAS tied to it
exp: Policy-based SAS inherit the policy's constraints; change or delete the policy to adjust or revoke them all.

q: How many stored access policies can you define per container?
exp: A container, share, queue, or table can have at most 5 stored access policies.

q: Which SAS type is signed with Microsoft Entra credentials instead of the storage account key?
exp: A user delegation SAS is secured with a user delegation key obtained via Entra ID.

q: A user delegation SAS can be created for which service(s)?
exp: User delegation SAS is supported for Blob storage, including Data Lake Storage Gen2.

q: How many access keys does a storage account have, and why?
opts: 2, so you can rotate one key while clients use the other
exp: Two keys allow rotation without downtime.

q: Which service stores storage keys securely for applications and can help automate rotation?
opts: Azure Key Vault (plus a key expiration policy on the storage account)
exp: Key Vault stores and rotates secrets; storage accounts support a key expiration policy that reminds you to rotate.

q: Azure file share users must authenticate with their on-premises AD DS identities over SMB. Besides enabling AD DS authentication on the account, what must be configured for users to access files?
opts: Share-level permissions (RBAC roles such as Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor) AND NTFS permissions on files and directories
exp: Access requires both layers: share-level RBAC and NTFS ACLs.

q: Which THREE identity sources are supported for Azure Files SMB identity-based authentication?
exp: AD DS, Entra Domain Services, and Entra Kerberos are supported.

q: Which built-in role allows reading blob data using Entra ID authentication, without granting account management rights?
exp: Storage Blob Data Reader is the data-plane read role. Storage Account Contributor is control-plane.

q: A user with the Reader role on a storage account browses blobs in the portal using 'Microsoft Entra user account' authentication. What happens?
opts: Access denied to blob data, because Reader is a control-plane role
exp: Control-plane Reader doesn't grant data access; a Storage Blob Data role is needed.

q: To let anyone on the internet read blobs by URL without listing the container, set the container's anonymous access level to:
exp: Blob = anonymous read of blobs only. Container also allows listing.

q: Answer Yes or No to each statement:
stmts: Regenerating an account key invalidates every SAS signed with it
A SAS can grant more permissions than the stored access policy it references
Unless exceptions are configured, the storage firewall applies to all networks, including Azure services
Entra ID authentication is supported for Blob and Queue data operations
exp: A key rotation kills its SAS tokens; SAS can only narrow a policy; the firewall applies broadly; Blob and Queue support Entra auth.

q: Which storage account type should you create for general scenarios that need blobs, files, queues, and tables with all redundancy options?
exp: GPv2 supports all services, tiers, and redundancy options.

q: You need the lowest latency for an SMB file share used by a database workload. Which account kind?
exp: Premium file shares run on FileStorage accounts (SSD-backed).

q: Which redundancy option keeps three copies of data within a single datacenter only?
exp: LRS keeps 3 synchronous copies in one datacenter.

q: Data must survive a full region outage AND the app must be able to read from the secondary region at any time. Minimum redundancy?
exp: RA-GRS adds read access to the secondary. A plain GRS secondary is readable only after failover.

q: Which redundancy option replicates synchronously across three availability zones in the primary region AND asynchronously to a secondary region?
exp: GZRS = ZRS in the primary + geo-replication to the secondary.

q: During a prolonged primary-region outage on a GRS account, who can initiate the failover, and what is the redundancy afterwards?
opts: The customer can initiate it; the account becomes LRS in the new primary region
exp: Customer-managed failover is available; afterwards the account is LRS until you re-enable geo-redundancy.

q: Which redundancy options can a Premium (block blob / file) storage account use?
exp: Premium accounts support LRS and ZRS (in supported regions), with no geo options.

q: Object replication between two storage accounts requires which prerequisites?
opts: Blob versioning on source and destination, and change feed on the source
Both accounts in the same region
exp: Versioning on both accounts and change feed on the source are required.

q: Which statement best describes object replication?
opts: Synchronous copy of all blob types
Asynchronous copy of block blobs between accounts, which can be in different regions or subscriptions
exp: Object replication copies block blobs asynchronously across accounts.

q: Azure Storage service-side encryption at rest is:
opts: Always enabled and cannot be disabled
exp: SSE with Microsoft-managed keys is always on.

q: To use customer-managed keys for a storage account, the key vault must have which two protections enabled?
exp: CMK requires soft delete and purge protection on the vault.

q: Infrastructure (double) encryption for a storage account can be enabled:
opts: Any time in the Encryption blade
exp: Infrastructure encryption is a creation-time setting.

q: Which AzCopy command uploads C:\data to a container and copies only files that changed since last time?
exp: azcopy sync compares source and destination and transfers differences.

q: AzCopy can authenticate to Blob storage using:
opts: Entra ID (azcopy login) or SAS tokens
exp: AzCopy supports Entra ID login and SAS tokens.

q: Azure Storage Explorer is best described as:
opts: A free cross-platform desktop app to manage blobs, files, queues, tables, and Data Lake
exp: Storage Explorer is a free desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

q: You must copy 60 TB of data to Azure from a site with very low bandwidth. The practical option is:
opts: Azure Import/Export or Azure Data Box (ship physical drives)
RDP file copy to a VM
exp: Offline transfer is designed for large datasets over limited bandwidth.

q: Answer Yes or No to each statement:
stmts: A storage account name must be globally unique, 3–24 characters, lowercase letters and numbers only
You can change LRS to GRS on a standard GPv2 account without recreating it
A storage account can be moved to another resource group
The account's default access tier (hot/cool) applies to Azure file shares
exp: Naming rules, in-place redundancy changes, and RG moves are supported; blob access tiers don't apply to file shares.

q: Azure Files SMB shares use which port, which many ISPs block?
exp: SMB uses TCP 445.

q: On-premises users can't reach an SMB file share because the ISP blocks port 445. What's a practical solution?
opts: Use VPN/ExpressRoute (or Azure File Sync) so SMB doesn't go directly over the internet
exp: Tunnel SMB over VPN/ExpressRoute with a private endpoint, or cache locally with Azure File Sync.

q: Which file share protocol is available only on premium (FileStorage) accounts and is used from Linux?
exp: NFS 4.1 shares require premium FileStorage accounts.

q: What is the correct hierarchy of Azure File Sync components?
opts: Storage Sync Service → sync group → one cloud endpoint + server endpoints
Storage Sync Service → server endpoint → many cloud endpoints per group
exp: Each sync group has exactly one cloud endpoint (an Azure file share) and one or more server endpoints.

q: What does cloud tiering in Azure File Sync do?
opts: Moves blobs to the archive tier
Keeps frequently used files on the local server while cold files become pointers, with full copies in Azure
exp: Cloud tiering caches hot files locally and replaces cold files with stubs that are recalled on access.

q: Which blob type is used for virtual machine disks (VHDs)?
exp: Page blobs handle random read/write workloads such as VHDs.

q: Which access tier is offline, so a blob can't be read until it's rehydrated?
exp: Archive is the only offline tier.

q: Rehydrating an archived blob with Standard priority typically takes:
exp: Standard priority takes up to 15 hours; High priority can finish in under an hour for blobs under 10 GB.

q: What are the early-deletion periods for the cool, cold, and archive tiers?
exp: Cool 30, cold 90, archive 180 days.

q: Which tiers can be set as the default account-level access tier?
exp: The default account tier is hot or cool. Archive (and cold) are set at the blob level.

q: Blobs should move to cool after 30 days without modification, to archive after 90, and be deleted after 365. What do you configure?
opts: A lifecycle management policy with rules based on last modified time
exp: Lifecycle management rules can tier and delete based on age.

q: After you create a new lifecycle management rule, roughly how long until its actions first run?
exp: A new policy can take up to 24 hours to take effect, and a run can take additional time.

q: What's the key difference between blob versioning and blob snapshots?
opts: Versioning creates a version automatically on every write or delete; snapshots are manual point-in-time copies
Snapshots are automatic; versions are manual
exp: Versioning is automatic, while snapshots are created explicitly.

q: Blob soft delete is set to 14 days. What does that mean?
opts: Deleted blobs can be undeleted within 14 days
Blobs can't be deleted for 14 days
The container is locked for 14 days
exp: Soft delete keeps deleted data recoverable for the retention period.

q: Share snapshots for Azure Files are:
opts: Read-only point-in-time copies of the whole share, incremental in storage use
Full copies billed at 100% each time
Automatic every hour and not configurable
exp: Share snapshots are read-only and incremental.

ctx: Invoices (block blobs) are stored in a GPv2 RA-GRS account. They must be instantly readable for 6 months and retained 7 years total. Instant access isn't needed after 6 months.
q: Which tier strategy is cheapest for months 7–84?
opts: Move to archive with a lifecycle rule after 6 months
exp: Archive is the cheapest storage tier for long retention when instant access isn't required. Lifecycle rules automate the move.
